The source text is `it('title'`, so `it'` matches nothing. Both sides of that diff extracted ZERO titles, the diff compared empty against empty, and it exited 0 on any tree whatsoever — including one where all ten cases had been deleted from the survivor. I reproduced this verbatim: on unmodified main the v5 pattern returns 0 matches on weekly-end-date.test.ts and 0 inside the scoped range of custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, and `diff` between them prints nothing and exits 0. I then applied the whole change, deleted the entire `weekly grouped report end bound` describe (three of the ten cases) from the survivor, and re-ran the v5 command on that broken tree: still EXIT=0 with no output — it passes exactly the defect the criterion exists to catch. The check was observed FAILING before it was observed passing, in both directions. While verifying that, I found a SECOND route to the same vacuous pass and removed it too: v5's command used `D=...` and `$D`, and when `$D` is unset — which is what happens if QA copies only the `diff` line — git and sed fail on stderr while `diff` still compares two empty streams and exits 0. Every claim below that used the old pattern's vacuous exit code as evidence has been struck and replaced with these runs: nothing here now asserts a check is 'verified to exit 0' on the strength of either defect. v5's own `understanding`, `debate_summary` and `alternatives_considered` already quoted the working pattern in their unscoped form, so the first defect was confined to the two commands that actually execute. So the epic's 'fold back whatever it uniquely adds' resolves one way: the 338-line file contributes nothing unique and is deleted outright. A repo-wide grep for 'weekly-end-date' over source, config and CI files returns nothing, and vitest discovers tests by the glob at packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts:406, so nothing has to be unlisted along with the deletion.

acceptance.how_to_verify:
Run this one command, which compares only the weekly end-bound cases rather than the whole file. Two things about it are load-bearing. (1) The pattern is `it\('` — the literal `(` after `it` is REQUIRED. v5 omitted it, which made the extraction yield zero titles and the command exit 0 on any tree at all. (2) The paths are written out in full, with NO shell variable. v5 also used `D=` and `$D`, and when `$D` is unset — which happens if only the `diff` line is copied — git and sed fail on stderr while `diff` still compares two empty streams and exits 0: the same vacuous pass by a second route. Full paths leave nothing to mistype:

diff <(git show main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+") \
     <(sed -n "/^describe(.weekly custom report end bound/,/^describe(.weekly budgeted report end bound/p" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+")

Run it from the repository root. It must print nothing, print NOTHING on stderr, and exit 0. Both sides are ten-title lists and they are equal. Sanity-check the pattern before trusting the result: `grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | wc -l` must print 23 for the whole file, and the same pattern piped through the sed range above must print 10. If either prints 0, the pattern has been mangled and the diff is meaningless; the wrong pattern `it'\K[^']+` prints 1 and 0 on those two, and that 0 is what made v5's version vacuous. This scoping is deliberate and not a regression: the whole file holds 23 `it('` titles, and diffing the branch file in full against main's ten prints `10a11,23` plus 13 extra titles and exits 1 even on a correct implementation, because those 13 belong to four describes out_of_scope forbids touching. The right-hand sed range is matched by describe NAME, not by line number, because the inserted comment block shifts every describe by +14 (the `weekly custom report end bound` describe is at 380 on main and 394 after this change). The range ends at the `describe` line itself, so the next describe's cases are excluded. This check was negative-tested in this run, not only observed passing: with the entire `weekly grouped report end bound` describe (three of the ten cases) removed from the survivor it prints `8,10d7` followed by the three missing titles and exits 1; with one title renamed inside the survivor it prints the old and new title and exits 1; on the correct tree it prints nothing and exits 0. If a shell mangles the nested quotes, the equivalent subset form — `comm -23 <(git show main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" | sort) <(grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | sort)` — also prints nothing and exits 0; prefer the diff, because the subset form is one-sided and would not notice a case renamed or added inside the two weekly describes. Separately, confirm no third file anywhere in the repo carries these titles: `git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" main -- packages` names exactly the two files being reconciled, and the same grep on the edited tree names only custom-spreadsheet.test.ts. Finally, `git diff -U0 main -- .../custom-spreadsheet.test.ts` shows no removed line, so no assertion inside the ten cases was touched.

Verifying that also surfaced a second vacuous-pass route nobody had flagged (the `$D` shell variable), which I hit by accident and then removed by writing the paths out in full. The passing direction was confirmed separately: no output on stdout, none on stderr, exit 0. v5's technical findings were re-derived from scratch and all hold — 10 titles in the deleted file, 23 in the survivor, identical ten, 76 changed lines in the describe-block diff with zero assertion lines, the 7/3 split in both files, the md5-identical fixture, 194 titles in the directory on main and 184 after, 14 added and 0 removed content lines in the survivor's diff, the resulting layout at 380-394, and step 3's single expected hit with the flag-order hazard reproduced at 4 hits. The residual 4 is that vitest cannot be executed in this checkout (no node_modules state file), so the test-count deltas in AC-1 and AC-5 are specified as measurements to take against main; AC-1's static half, which needs no suite and which was run here, shows 194 and 184.
evidence: Objection reproduced verbatim, on unmodified main with no change applied. The v5 pattern `grep -oP "it'\K[^']+"` returns 0 matches on weekly-end-date.test.ts, 1 on the whole of custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, and 0 inside the scoped sed range. `diff <(git show main:$D/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it'\K[^']+") <(sed -n "/^describe(.weekly custom report end bound/,/^describe(.weekly budgeted report end bound/p" $D/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -oP "it'\K[^']+")` compares empty against empty, prints nothing and exits 0.

The v5 command on a deliberately broken tree still passes, which is the defect. With the whole change applied and the entire `weekly grouped report end bound` describe (three of the ten cases) removed from the survivor, that same v5 command printed nothing and returned EXIT=0 — it passed the exact defect AC-4 exists to catch.

The corrected command on that same broken tree fails correctly: it printed `8,10d7` followed by `applies the same bound as the custom spreadsheet`, `clamps to today the same way the custom spreadsheet does` and `widens a week-start end date in the table view too`, and returned EXIT=1.

The corrected command on a rename fails correctly: with `clamps to today while the final week is still in progress` renamed to `clamps to today when the final week is unfinished` inside the survivor, it printed `3c3` with both titles and returned EXIT=1. Restoring the file returned EXIT=0. The check therefore has teeth in both directions, which is the verification the rejection asked for and which the v5 command never had.

A SECOND vacuous-pass route was found while re-verifying the first, and is now also removed. v5's command used `D=...` and `$D`. Running its `diff` line without the variable set — which is what happens if QA copies only that line — produced `fatal: path '/weekly-end-date.test.ts' does not exist in 'main'` and `sed: can't read /custom-spreadsheet.test.ts` on stderr and still returned EXIT=0, because both process substitutions produced empty streams. This run happened to produce it accidentally while scripting the extraction. AC-4 and qa_script step 2 now write both paths out in full with no shell variable, and the variable-free form was verified to give EXIT=0 on the correct tree and EXIT=1 with `8,10d7` on the three-cases-removed tree.

Pattern sanity counts, on the correct applied tree: `grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | wc -l` is 23, and the same pattern through the scoped sed range is 10. AC-4 and qa_script step 2 both require these two numbers before the diff is trusted, so a mangled pattern fails the step instead of passing it.

The command was also run as extracted programmatically from the finished work-order.json, not retyped, to confirm the pattern survives JSON encoding: the JSON stores `grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+"`, which decodes to the correct regex, and executing the decoded text gave EXIT=0 on the correct tree and EXIT=1 with `8,10d7` on the broken tree.

Left-hand titles from `git show main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+"` and right-hand titles from the scoped range were printed side by side and are the same ten strings in the same order.
The 7/3 split holds in the survivor's two weekly describes (7 and 3) and in the deleted file (7 and 3).

`diff <(sed -n '181,338p' .../weekly-end-date.test.ts) <(sed -n '380,549p' custom-spreadsheet.test.ts)` — `grep -c '^[<>]'` returns 76, and piping those 76 lines through `grep -cE 'expect|toEqual|toBe|toHave'` returns 0, so no assertion, expected value or snapshot line differs anywhere.
`sed -n '36,47p' weekly-end-date.test.ts | md5sum` and `sed -n '43,54p' custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | md5sum` — both 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 (the weeklyRows fixture).

Applied the change and measured the result: `git diff -U0 main -- .../custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -cE '^\+[^+ ]|^[+]$'` returns 14 and `grep -cE '^-[^- ]|^[-]$'` returns 0 — 13 comment lines plus the blank separator, nothing removed. Layout is 378 `});`, 379 blank, 380-392 the block, 393 blank, 394 the `describe`.

grep -n '^describe(' on both files — custom-spreadsheet.test.ts on main: 380, 504, 551, 644, 802, 954; weekly-end-date.test.ts: 181 and 293. On the applied tree the survivor's describes are at 394, 518, 565, 658, 816, 968 — every one shifted by exactly +14.

Comment block measured line by line on the applied tree: 13 lines (380-392); widths 58, 2, 74, 75, 52, 2, 71, 76, 77, 75, 58, 2, 71, longest 77, within oxfmt printWidth 80 (.oxfmtrc.json); the token `weekly-end-date` appears on line 382 only, and that is the block's third line.

qa_script step 3 measured both ways with a work-order.json and a previous-output.json at the repo root, as the pipeline leaves them: excludes AFTER includes yields exactly 1 hit (custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:382) and exit 0; the same flags placed BEFORE the includes yields 4 hits (work-order.json twice, previous-output.json once, plus the comment). GNU grep applies --include/--exclude last-one-wins.

Static test-count delta, which needs no suite: the nine test files in packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/ hold 194 `it('` titles on main and 184 after the change — exactly ten fewer. All nine files are flat in that directory, so the git ls-tree loop and `grep -hP ... $D/*.test.ts` count the same set. Both numbers were run in the applied tree.

`git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" main -- packages` names exactly the two files being reconciled; the same grep on the edited tree names only custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.
grep -rn 'weekly-end-date' over the whole repo excluding node_modules, .git and plan — no hit in any source, config or CI file; the only hits are in plan/, which quotes the rejected plans.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts and move anything unique into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is nothing to move. The diff over the two describe blocks contains no assertion line at all, the ten titles are identical, and the bodies differ only in the props wrapper, whose defaults the shorter file already supplied. This was the epic's first option and it reduces to a plain delete.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts and delete the ten cases from custom-spreadsheet.test.ts instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps the weaker of the two suites. The survivor would lose the server double that applies `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, and it would strand the `weeklyProps` helper, which the weekly budgeted describe also uses. It also means editing a 1100-line file to delete ten cases rather than deleting a 338-line file outright.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract the ten cases plus their fixtures and server double into a shared test helper both files import.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves both files running the same ten cases, which is the duplication the ticket exists to remove — it hides the duplication behind an import instead of ending it, and it adds a shared helper to a codebase trying to lose a file, not gain a layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts but mark the ten cases `it.skip`, or move them under a single shared describe imported by both.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Skipped tests still count in a reportable total, so AC-1's 'drops by exactly ten' would fail; and the shared-describe form keeps two files alive for one suite. Either leaves the 338 lines a reviewer is asked to judge, which the ticket names as half the cost.

alternatives_considered.approach: Record the comparison in both the code comment and the release note, as v1's AC-2/AC-3/qa_script step 6 required.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the objection v1 was rejected for. It cannot be carried out by the implementer: the repo's release-note convention says one sentence, and the existing precedent for a Maintenance note of this kind is a single clause with no narrative. Requiring both means the release note either violates the repo convention or fails the plan's own acceptance criteria. The obligation is therefore narrowed to the code comment.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep v2's bare repo-wide grep and add an explicit exemption list naming the comment block and the release-note filename.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the objection v2 was rejected for, and the list would be a third artefact that must be kept in step with files[1] and AC-2 — the same failure mode a third time. Scoping the grep by file type makes the two required mentions invisible to the check by construction, so there is nothing to keep in step.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the reviewer's alternative on the comment text: drop the 'exactly the text supplied' clause from files[1] and rewrite AC-2 to require only the content, without pinning an opening phrase.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the disagreement but leaves the implementer choosing the wording, which is a judgement call the planner exists to remove — and AC-2 would then be judged by a QA agent with no memory of the implementer's reasoning. Quoting the block in full costs 13 lines and makes both artefacts point at one text.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrite files[1]'s comment block so the token falls on its fourth line, leaving v3's AC-2 ordinal as written.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer's required fix was explicit that the block must not be edited to chase the ordinal, because the block is the artefact AC-2 is judged against for the character-for-character match. Reordering the block to satisfy an ordinal would also read as fitting the prose to the checker. AC-2 was corrected to say third line instead, and files[1] quotes a block whose third line it is.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix AC-4 and qa_script step 2 with the reviewer's SECOND option — keep the whole-file extraction and state the real relation as a subset check, `comm -23 <(main titles | sort) <(branch titles | sort)` printing nothing.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works and was verified on the applied tree, but it is one-sided: it proves every title from main survived into the survivor and says nothing about the survivor's own two weekly describes, so a case added or renamed there would pass. The reviewer's first option — scope to the two describes and diff the two ten-title lists — fails in both directions (verified this run: a rename inside the survivor is caught, exit 1) and keeps the check's stated result the same shape as the thing being checked. The subset form is offered in both artefacts as a quoting escape hatch only.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix AC-4 and step 2 by scoping the right-hand extraction with hardcoded line numbers (`sed -n '380,549p'` on main's numbering) rather than by describe name.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works only before the change. This change inserts 14 lines above line 380, so the same command run after the change starts inside the comment block and ends 45 lines early. Any command that locates a describe by line number has to be written twice; matching on the name works once.

alternatives_considered.approach: Answer the last objection by keeping v4's qa_script step 3 exactly as written, including its trailing `grep -v` and its note that the pipeline exits 1 on success.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works, but running it here showed the exit code belongs to the second grep rather than to the search — the first grep legitimately matches the mandated comment — so a QA agent reading exit 1 would fail a passing check. Collapsing it to one grep with exactly one expected hit, whose full text is given, removes the trap and makes the expectation sharper: it proves both that nothing else referenced the deleted file and that the survivor's only hit is the mandated comment.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the rejected pattern by changing the regex to something that cannot be mis-transcribed, e.g. `grep -oP "it\(?'\K[^']+"` or a `sed -n "s/^\s*it('\(.*\)',.*/\1/p"` form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: An optional-paren regex silently tolerates the exact omission that caused the rejection — it would match in a file that lacks the parenthesis, which is a different file shape, and it hides a transcription error rather than surfacing it. The `sed` capture form avoids backslashes entirely and is tempting, but it is anchored on `it('` at line start with a specific trailing `',` and would need re-checking against every one of the ten call sites' formatting; the reviewer asked for the pattern to be corrected, not swapped for a second pattern needing its own verification. Instead the plan keeps the exact corrected pattern AND requires the sanity counts (23 and 10) before the diff is trusted, which is what catches a mis-transcription.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the `D=`/`$D` variable in AC-4 and qa_script step 2 for readability, and rely on the sanity counts alone to catch a mistyped path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The sanity counts do not catch it. This run showed that an unset `$D` produces error output on stderr and still EXIT=0 from the diff, while the sanity count command — which QA may well run with its own correctly-set variable — prints the expected 23 and 10. The check would pass while comparing nothing. Writing both paths out in full removes the failure mode instead of trying to detect it, and the paths are stable: they are named in the delete instruction and in the diff anyway.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: v5 was rejected on one objection and the objection is right, and it is a serious one: AC-4.how_to_verify and qa_script step 2 each wrote the title extraction as `grep -oP "it'\K[^']+"`, missing the literal `(`. Both sides of that diff therefore extracted zero titles, the diff compared empty against empty, and it exited 0 on any tree at all. I reproduced this verbatim on unmodified main, then applied the whole change, deleted the entire `weekly grouped report end bound` describe — three of the ten cases — from the survivor, and re-ran v5's command on that broken tree: still no output, still EXIT=0. It passes exactly the defect the criterion exists to catch. Two supporting measurements confirm the diagnosis rather than infer it: the pattern `it'\K[^']+` yields 0 on the deleted file and 0 inside the scoped range, and v5's own prose elsewhere (understanding, debate_summary, alternatives_considered, and the comm -23 escape hatch in both artefacts) already used the working `it\('` form — so only the two commands that actually execute were broken. Both the pattern and the two sentences claiming the extraction 'yields exactly 10 titles' are corrected: with `it\('` it yields 10 in the scoped range and 23 in the whole file, with `it'` it yields 0 and 1. The reviewer's required verification in the failing direction is now done, not asserted: with the corrected pattern and three cases removed the command prints `8,10d7` plus the three missing titles and exits 1; with one title renamed inside the survivor it prints the old and new title and exits 1; on the correct tree it prints nothing and exits 0. Verifying this surfaced a SECOND route to the same vacuous pass, which nobody had flagged: v5's command used `D=`/`$D`, and running the `diff` line without that variable set — what happens when only that line is copied — errors on stderr and still exits 0, because both process substitutions yield empty streams. The sanity counts do not catch this, since QA may run those with its own correctly-set variable. Both AC-4 and step 2 now write the paths out in full with no shell variable, and the variable-free form was itself verified in both directions. Every 'verified to exit 0' / 'verified twice' claim that rested on the vacuous run is struck and replaced by these paired observations. To keep a mis-transcription from silently reintroducing either defect, AC-4 and step 2 both require the sanity counts — 23 for the whole file, 10 for the scoped range — before the diff is trusted. Nothing else in v5 changed: the technical finding was re-derived from scratch and holds — 76 changed lines in the describe-block diff with zero assertion lines, 7/3 split identical in both files, fixture md5-identical, 194 `it('` titles in the directory on main and 184 after, 14 added and 0 removed content lines in the survivor's diff, and the resulting layout at 378-394. Step 3's flag-order hazard was re-measured with a realistic work-order.json at the repo root (1 hit in the correct order, 4 in the reversed order) rather than assumed. The v1 through v4 fixes are kept intact — the comparison lives in exactly one artefact, the release note is one sentence by repo convention, and files[1] quotes the comment verbatim so AC-2 and files[1] cannot disagree. The working tree was reverted after the verification run.
residual_risks: The vitest halves of AC-1 and AC-5 are the only claims here not directly executed, because this checkout has no node_modules state and vitest cannot start. Both are stated as measurements to take against main. The static half of AC-1 — 194 `it('` titles across the directory on main, 184 after — was executed here and needs no suite.

A QA agent who retypes AC-4's command from memory rather than copying it could reintroduce either vacuous-pass fault (a mangled pattern, or an unset path). The required sanity counts (23 and 10) catch the first; the second is removed by writing the paths in full rather than mitigated.
